query: Which material can be used for to improve the ductility and toughness of the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy (HEAs), and why?

generation.hypothesis: Adding 0.5-1.0 at% Boron to the HfZrTi high-entropy alloy will enhance its ductility and toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: The base HfZrTi high-entropy alloy exhibits limited ductility and toughness, with brittle characteristics under standard conditions.
generation.conditions: Standard testing conditions, such as ambient temperature mechanical loading.
generation.mechanism: At low concentrations, Boron is expected to segregate to the grain boundaries, enhancing their cohesion and stability. This grain-boundary engineering minimizes brittleness and improves load transfer during deformation, leading to enhanced ductility and toughness.
generation.predicted_outcome: Observable improvements in ductility and toughness, such as increased elongation at failure and higher fracture toughness, compared to the pristine HfZrTi alloy.
generation.baseline: HfZrTi HEA without any Boron doping, which serves as a reference for its current mechanical performance.
generation.boundary: The improvement should hold as long as the Boron concentration remains within 0.5-1.0 at%; exceeding this range could lead to unwanted second-phase formation or other deleterious effects.
generation.uncertainty: The precise quantitative improvements in mechanical properties remain uncertain until further experimental validation is performed.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of HfZrTi HEA samples: one set with 0.5-1.0 at% Boron doping and another set as the undoped control. Conduct mechanical testing at ambient temperature including tensile and fracture toughness evaluations.
measurements: Tensile stress-strain analysis (to measure ductility and yield strength)
Microstructural analysis via TEM/EDS to confirm Boron segregation at grain boundaries
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Boron-doped HEA does not exhibit statistically significant improvements in ductility and fracture toughness, or if microstructural analysis fails to detect Boron segregation at the grain boundaries, then the hypothesis is falsified.

levers.principle: Even at a very low concentration, Boron tends to segregate at grain boundaries, enhancing their cohesion and stability. This grain-boundary engineering minimizes brittleness and aids in better load transfer during deformation, which in turn improves the ductility and toughness.

Nb enters the HfZrTi matrix to provide solid solution strengthening while stabilizing a more ductile BCC-type phase. This addition improves dislocation mobility and reduces intrinsic brittleness without disrupting the high-entropy balance.

The intentional addition of Cu can promote the formation of a secondary FCC phase, which is inherently more ductile. This dual-phase microstructure helps to arrest crack propagation and enhances the overall toughness of the alloy while being chemically compatible.

Mo acts as an effective solid solution strengthener and can refine the internal microstructure. Its addition improves dislocation interactions and promotes a more uniform plastic deformation behavior, thereby increasing ductility and toughness under ambient conditions.
